evals.name: small-service
evals.prompt: Design a Go service with config, a shared DB pool, an order store, order logic, and HTTP handlers. No framework is selected. Show package boundaries, constructor signatures and startup failure ownership. Does this need clean architecture and a DI library?

assertions.text: Recommends simple manual wiring without a size-based framework mandate.
Places necessary interface contracts at consumers without demanding interfaces for every dependency.
Distinguishes shared pool ownership and cleans up successful acquisitions if later construction fails.

evals.name: options-validation
evals.prompt: Design the constructor for a Go client with optional minimum and maximum delays. Options may be supplied in any order and min must not exceed max. Compare a config struct and functional options.

assertions.text: Allows both config struct and options with stated tradeoffs rather than mandating options.
Validates the final min/max pair after defaults and options, not just each option independently.

evals.name: zero-and-enums
evals.prompt: Can private fields plus a NewStatus constructor make invalid Go Status values impossible? Would type Status int and three iota constants solve it?

assertions.text: Explains zero-valued structs remain constructible.
Explains named integer enums admit undeclared values and defines boundary or operation validation.

evals.name: api-compatibility
evals.prompt: Review a proposed Go API change: NewStore used to return a public Store interface; now it returns *store. The author says accept interfaces, return structs makes this automatically compatible.

assertions.text: Rejects automatic compatibility, including assignments to function types or callers relying on the old signature.
Treats interface return as possibly intentional rather than inherently wrong.

evals.name: embedding
evals.prompt: Our Go Envelope embeds a dependency that just added MarshalJSON. Envelope has its own exported fields and tags. Is embedding only a code-reuse detail?

assertions.text: Explains promoted marshaling methods can change serialization of the outer type.
Suggests named-field delegation or explicit marshaling and a wire-output check.

evals.name: copy-contract
evals.prompt: Design Snapshot() for a Go registry storing map[string][]*Item. Callers must be free to mutate results without changing registry state. Is maps.Clone enough?

assertions.text: Says map cloning is shallow and slices and pointed-to items still alias.
Copies all mutable layers promised independent or changes the contract explicitly.

evals.name: generic-keys
evals.prompt: Review a generic Set[K comparable] map[K]struct{} instantiated as Set[any]. Is inserting []int{1} safe because the generic type compiled?

assertions.text: Explains dynamic unhashable values can still panic with an interface key.
Proposes an explicit accepted-key contract or boundary check without claiming generics prove runtime comparability.

evals.name: di-runtime
evals.prompt: A proposal says samber/do generics prove all providers exist and eliminate cycles at compile time, while Fx instantiates all registered providers eagerly. Review these claims.

assertions.text: Rejects compile-time graph completeness for samber/do.
Explains provider demand in Fx and separates compilation from graph/startup validation.

evals.name: di-scope
evals.prompt: Our Go application has a DB pool, a stateless validator and tenant-specific request data. Should all stateful services be singletons, all stateless services transient, and every dependency lazy?

assertions.text: Chooses scopes from lifetime and isolation rather than statefulness alone.
Explains required readiness checks versus optional lazy work and first-use failure costs.

evals.name: aggregate-failure
evals.prompt: An Order.Add method appends an item and then validates the new total, returning error on overflow. Place then saves the order and publishes an event. Review the design boundaries.

assertions.text: Identifies failed mutation leaving invalid in-memory state.
Does not treat save then publish as atomic; names a consistency mechanism or explicit failure contract.

evals.name: presence
evals.prompt: Design a Go 1.23 PATCH request field whose absent, null and numeric zero meanings differ. Will omitzero alone preserve all three?

assertions.text: Does not use Go 1.24 omitzero as a Go 1.23 solution.
Distinguishes presence from value and proposes custom decoding or an explicit presence representation.

evals.name: iterator-contract
evals.prompt: Design a Go 1.23 API for lazy records from a closeable source. A caller may stop early and the source may return an error after its last record.

assertions.text: Specifies release on early termination and obeying yield false.
Preserves terminal errors and describes deferred errors or repeatability.
